nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier.

nodes.entity_id: Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering Approach
nodes.description: A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages and present potentially misclassified messages to the user.
nodes.id: Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering Approach

nodes.description: A model generated during the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, maintained within memory on a user's client device as memory resident only, and not stored on disk or in another persistent data store.

A message filter that assigns messages to different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store; it is automatically executed independent of a user action.<SEP>A previously applied message filter that sorts messages into various folders for a user and is configured to store first classification data in a persistent store.

A filter configured to generate a classification model based on a first pass analysis and to perform a second pass on sorted messages to generate a misclassification identification of sorted messages.

A device configured to receive messages, assign them to different message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over a network to the message folders.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform actions for managing delivery of a message over a network.
A component of the network device used to send and receive data over a network.
A component of the network device operative to perform actions including first pass analysis, second pass analysis, displaying misclassification identification, and purging the classification model.

A communication item received in plurality, assigned to message folders, scored by the multi-pass message filter, and potentially identified as sorted into an incorrect message folder.<SEP>An email or similar item delivered over a network that is sorted into message folders and analyzed by message filters.
A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by a message filter and to which misclassified messages can be moved.
A memory location where the generated classification model resides exclusively, from which the model is purged and not stored on disk or another persistent data store.
A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.

A device that executes the multi-pass message filter, generates and stores second classification data in a non-persistent memory store, identifies incorrectly sorted messages, and displays information enabling a user to move messages to another folder.<SEP>A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may execute entirely.
A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.
A classifier employed by the multi-pass message filter.
An identification of sorted messages generated by the second pass, displayed so that at least one misclassified message can be moved to a different message folder.
An analysis performed on a plurality of messages previously sorted into folders, used to train the multi-pass message filter and generate a classification model.
A pass using the generated classification model on the sorted messages to score each message and identify misclassified messages.
Information within messages read during the first pass, including sender address and whether the sender's address is in an address book associated with a recipient.
Information within messages read during the first pass, including a subject and an originating network address.
The content of messages read during the first pass analysis.
Attachments within messages read during the first pass analysis.

A book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders; a message sender's address in the address book may be analyzed to generate second classification data.<SEP>An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in analysis of whether a message sender's address is present.

A person enabled to move an identified message to another message folder and able to select execution of the multi-pass message filter through an interface on the client device.<SEP>A person for whom messages are sorted into folders and who is presented a list of potentially misclassified messages and enabled to move identified messages to another folder.
An interface on the client device through which a user can select the multi-pass message filter for execution.

A message filter executed in multiple passes on sorted messages; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass uses that data to score each message and identify messages sorted into incorrect message folders.
A folder into which messages are sorted; messages may be identified as stored in an incorrect message folder and moved to another message folder.
Classification data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter when assigning messages to message folders.

Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train it; it resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory store at the client device and is deleted upon providing the display of information.
A memory store at the client device where the second classification data resides exclusively.
A communications network over which messages are communicated to the message folders.
